customManagers.description: skalibs, pinned by commit with its tag as a comment. skarnet versions are A.B.C.D, which semver-coerced cannot order (it offered only same-tag digest updates), so the versioning says so: a change in B is skarnet's incompatible bump and arrives as a Renovate 'minor'.
s6, pinned the same way as skalibs.

xpra -- the display server the native Porthole viewer speaks to -- installed into the shared base image from xpra.org (it is not in Debian). XPRA_VERSION is the ONE place the image's version lives: base/Dockerfile takes it as a build arg and pins the whole xpra package SET with it. Ships-if-green like every other bump in the org: base-image.yml builds the image on the PR, and a protocol regression is fixed forward in the next dated release. The runtime canary is the launcher's check_xpra_compat, which compares a container's xpra against what the VIEWER speaks (PortholeClient.m's hello, deliberately NOT this pin) and nudges a rebuild when they diverge.
clang22, the family compiler every Porthole Mac binary is built with (cmake/MavericksClang22Toolchain.cmake, build/fetch-s6.sh); one bare release tag.

packageRules.description: skalibs and s6 move in ONE PR: each s6 release is built against its own skalibs (s6 2.15 is an 'adaptation to skalibs-2.15'), so either bump alone fails to build and neither could ever land. Not an automerge exception -- automerge is the family default (ship-if-green) and still applies; build/check-transport.sh is what makes green mean 'the shipped s6-ipcserver works', not merely 'it compiled'.

Held below 2.15 until skarnet releases skalibs 879e42b (2026-11-04, 'Only report POLLHUP on EOF/error in iopause_select'). Every released skalibs >= 2.15 uses select() on macOS and reports POLLHUP on every readable fd, so s6-ipcserverd dies on its first event ('trouble with socket'); build/check-transport.sh catches it. 2.14.x still flows. Remove this rule (and its check in tests/renovate_test.sh) once a release carries the fix.
